title: Synthetic calibration, uncertainty, missingness, subgroup, temporal-sensitivity, and abstention propagation contracts
objective: Implement a replaceable public synthetic framework that evaluates calibration mechanics where probability outputs exist, preserves exact uncertainty and missingness states, reports subgroup and temporal sensitivity without sparse-cell overclaim, and propagates abstention through the exact-ten decision boundary.
business_reason: Commercial-value and policy decisions require explicit uncertainty and abstention semantics; point estimates from the baseline framework cannot be consumed safely until these contracts fail closed.
inputs: BASELINE-001 frozen cohort, policy registry, metrics, and replacement disposition
OUTCOMES-001 nullable label-state and common-as-of contracts
synthetic calibration and sensitivity fixtures only
non_goals: claim real calibration or predictive validity
estimate causal lift or commercial value
invent uncertainty intervals from one synthetic fixture
collapse sparse or missing subgroups into confident estimates
authorize production scoring, live ranking, or outreach
evaluator: freeze a public evaluator contract before material implementation
separate ranking scores from probability-valued outputs
exact calibration-bin, coverage, missingness, subgroup, temporal, and abstention semantics
registered sparse-cell, future-label, pooled-subgroup, point-estimate-only, interval-overclaim, and abstention-loss mutations
known_bad_cases: uncalibrated rank score treated as probability
future or null label admitted to calibration
empty or sparse bin reported as precise
micro aggregation represented as route-day macro behavior
subgroup disparity hidden by pooled aggregation
synthetic interval represented as empirical confidence
abstention dropped or coerced to a negative outcome
test labels reused for calibrator selection
acceptance: probability eligibility and calibration mechanics use one strict point-in-time interface
null labels, missing features, sparse cells, and abstentions retain explicit non-computable states
route-day macro and micro metrics are separately named and exact
subgroup and temporal outputs expose denominators and never imply empirical fairness or stability
all registered mutations are rejected by an evaluator independent from the builder
real calibration, predictive, causal, commercial, and production claims remain behind named gates
rollback: Remove the calibration framework and retain the validated BASELINE-001 nullable metrics and no-replacement disposition; invalidate dependent economics fixtures and keep live permissions disabled.
stop_budget: Remain synthetic and non-influencing; do not infer empirical reliability, subgroup fairness, stability, predictive value, lift, economics, or production fitness.
